papers.summary: Long-lived secure channels for embedded and cyber-physical systems (CPSs) must resist quantum attacks and failures in endpoint randomness. While several post-quantum key exchange protocols exist, their security assumes reliable randomness at the endpoint, but this assumption is not always true in embedded devices. In this paper, we introduce the Entropy Attack Suite (EAS) to evaluate secure channels facing endpoint randomness failures, such as low-entropy boot and Random Number Generation (RNG) path subversion. As a case study, we design and implement APQKE-DR, a post-quantum secure channel. Its handshake uses ML-KEM [1] and ML-DSA [2], producing a root key for an X25519 Double Ratchet. We assess the performance of APQKE-DR and security for smart grid communication, and integrate it beneath ANSI C12.22 and DNP3 without altering payload formats. On a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5, the APQKE handshake exchanges 9,610 bytes with median latencies of 1.99 ms (node) and 0.82 ms (server). The ratcheted channel adds 31 bytes per message. With fresh randomness and ideal cryptographic primitives, ProVerif verifies the modeled secrecy and authentication properties. If randomness fails, EAS can recover the RNG stream and root key from public transcripts. Under RNG-path subversion, a weak generator exposes the root key across sessions. If subversion also affects X25519 keys, attackers may access ratchet keys and plaintexts. TPM seeding prevents early-boot attacks but not later subversion, while measured boot can block modified firmware. Secure deployment thus requires integrity along the entire entropy path, not just strong cryptographic primitives.

papers.title: Bit-Flip Attacks on Quantized Neural Networks without Knowledge of Model Parameters
papers.summary: We show that quantization asymmetry concentrates bit-flip vulnerability in small tensors retained at high precision. CoarseHammer targets these tensors and accepts flips at any bit, without parameter values, gradients, or data. It remains effective under continued fine-tuning. Under ideal placement, CoarseHammer reaches chance accuracy in at least 81.5% of runs on each of ten evaluated models, including four large language models, with median successful runs requiring at most 24 flips. On simulated DRAM with 0.01 flippable bits per million, it outperforms three prior attacks on every evaluated convolutional network, succeeding in up to 83.6% of runs while they never succeed. On a real system, CoarseHammer steers heap-allocated tensors onto vulnerable frames despite address space layout randomization, without accessing the model file. With 16 templated frames, median accuracy reaches chance for all four language models and approximately chance for four convolutional networks.
papers.title_zh: 无需模型参数知识的量化神经网络比特翻转攻击
papers.abstract_zh: 我们表明，量化不对称性将比特翻转脆弱性集中在以高精度保留的小张量中。CoarseHammer 针对这些张量，并接受任意比特位上的翻转，无需参数值、梯度或数据。它在持续微调下仍然有效。在理想放置下，CoarseHammer 在十个被评估模型中的每一个上，至少有 81.5% 的运行达到随机水平准确率，其中包括四个大语言模型；成功运行的中位数至多需要 24 次翻转。在每百万比特中有 0.01 个可翻转比特的模拟 DRAM 上，它在每个被评估的卷积网络上均优于三种先前的攻击，在最高 83.6% 的运行中成功，而它们从未成功。在真实系统上，CoarseHammer 在地址空间布局随机化的情况下，将堆分配的张量引导到脆弱帧上，且无需访问模型文件。使用 16 个模板化帧时，四个语言模型的准确率中位数达到随机水平，四个卷积网络的准确率中位数接近随机水平。

papers.title: Encrypted Fixed-Point Multiplication in Quasilinear Complexity
papers.summary: Homomorphic encryption enables computation on encrypted data, but its high computational overhead remains a central obstacle. We overcome this obstacle asymptotically for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic. In this paper, we introduce focused encoding, which represents a fixed-point number of $n$-bit precision using a polynomial of degree $O(n/\log n)$ over a polynomially bounded modulus by concentrating precision at one embedding. We then introduce an error-shaping technique for homomorphic operations to preserve the encoding. This yields an encrypted fixed-point multiplication algorithm for the CKKS scheme that runs in online time $O(n \log n)$ at $n$-bit precision for any fixed multiplicative depth, with security parameter $λ= O(n/\log^2 n)$. Further, we develop bootstrapping for focused encoding to overcome the quadratic cost of conventional bootstrapping. We bootstrap ciphertext coefficients at an enlarged scale and shape the resulting error to preserve focused encoding, at the cost of additional modulus consumption. Then, to reduce the remaining logarithmic overhead, we decompose the ciphertext into components over a smaller subring and bootstrap each separately. This reduces the online cost per multiplication, including bootstrapping, to $O(n \log n + n (\log λ)^3 \log \log λ)$ for security parameter $λ= O(n/\log^3 n)$.

papers.title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
papers.summary: Request-derived authorizers such as Progent protect LLM agents from prompt injection by deriving what an agent may do from the user's request. Their guarantee rests on attribution: the request is taken to be what the user said. Compaction breaks it. At every automatic compaction we observed, Claude Code and Codex placed a model-written summary of earlier turns as a user message, so the compactor's quotation of the user, documents and injected text reads as the user speaking. Because a policy frozen at the first request lets the agent finish few later tasks, we let Progent derive its policy for each request, and find that what it grants then follows what the compactor wrote. Even a payee the user stated is not safe: when an attacker's notice states another account as plain data and the user asks to pay the rent, the policy derived from a frontier compactor's summary admits the notice's account in 91% of cases, and the one derived from the user's own words in none. The cause is general: we prove that an authorizer that cannot see who wrote which bytes cannot treat a forged record differently from the legitimate one it imitates by more than the two are distinguishable, and that the bound is tight. Frontier compactors bear this out: they mark injected instructions, which have no legitimate twin, but rarely injected data, which does. What a compactor keeps, and how it marks it, is a security parameter. The fix follows from attribution: the authorizer credits only what the user said, authenticated on arrival and carried verbatim across the boundary, while the agent still reads the summary. We prove that it then receives exactly that text or nothing, so an attacker can block the policy but cannot shape it, and adaptive attacks on our implementation confirm it. In 40 attacked AgentDojo episodes re-run with the fix, no attacker action completes while the agent reads the summary.

papers.title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
papers.summary: Coding agents let plugins and remote services answer permission prompts, and Claude Code documents that such an answer cannot override the operator's deny rules. However, we show that this guarantee, checked one decision at a time, fails over a whole run, because an answer to one permission prompt can rewrite the policy that every later answer is checked against. For example, a remote service with no access to the operator's files approves an unrelated command and attaches an update that deletes the deny rule protecting the project's secrets. The agent then reads the secrets in that session and the next, even inside the vendor's strict sandbox. The root cause is that Claude Code checks only updates that add or replace allow rules. Relays that forward such deletions already exist, including the vendor's own Remote Control. In effect, the right to answer a prompt has become the right to administer the policy. Worse, the deletion leaves the same records as a local edit by the operator, so Claude Code cannot tell who wrote a rule. More generally, what a runtime records decides what it can safely delegate. A runtime that cannot tell who wrote a rule can accept only updates that keep every currently denied call denied, whereas, to protect every party's restrictions, a runtime that records who wrote each rule can let each party remove only the restrictions proven to be its own. We prove that these two bounds are tight. They correctly predict whether the operator's restrictions survive in all thirteen permission designs across ten agent systems, including predictions we wrote down before running Codex, Gemini CLI, opencode, and Goose. Enforcing the bounds at the shared update step blocks the attack. A survey of 2,227 fetched marketplace plugins finds only two that send policy updates.

papers.title: Spoofing Wireless Sensing with Metasurfase-based Physical Deepfakes
papers.summary: Wireless communication networks are expanding from mere information transfer to sensing: in the Integrated Sensing and Communication paradigm, existing infrastructure and signals are reused to capture physical information about the surroundings of devices, envisioned to inform high-stakes applications such as healthcare and autonomous vehicles. From a security perspective, wireless sensing inherently trusts physical observations of the radio environment. However, as in wireless communication, the open nature of radio propagation allows attackers to tamper with victim signals. In particular, attackers can use programmable metasurfaces to manipulate wireless channels and thereby mislead sensing systems. Yet, prior metasurface-based manipulations target only individual channel features such as variance or Doppler shifts. Thus, they require knowledge of the victim sensing system and produce implausible channels that are easy to detect. In this work, we show that metasurfaces enable physically plausible manipulation of wireless sensing that is independent of the features used by the victim sensing system. Our attack reproduces genuine pre-recorded events at the physical layer and thereby synthesizes physical deepfakes of wireless channels. To this end, we develop an attack framework that controls the amplitude and phase of victim channels across time, frequency, and antennas. The key challenge here is to build a deep learning model of the interaction between metasurface and victim channel. We demonstrate that attackers can solve this challenge in several settings, e.g., by exploiting Wi-Fi Beamforming Feedback Information or replicating the victim environment. We validate the attack both in a controlled lab study on MIMO channels and with off-the-shelf Wi-Fi sensing. Our results fundamentally challenge the trustworthiness of wireless sensing.

papers.title: AgentBank: Banking on Blockchain Agentic Payments
papers.summary: AI agents increasingly pay for data and computation through protocols such as x402 and AP2, but individually funded wallets idle and require asset transfers for every payment. We present AgentBank, a smart-contract banking layer that lets agents spend bank liabilities under owner-issued mandates and on-chain spending limits. Internal payments update account balances without transferring assets, while pooled backing funds are allocated between reserves and yield-bearing strategies. We bound losses from compromised agent keys and analyze how correlated demand affects reserve requirements. Experiments show that AgentBank reduces idle liquidity by 52-77% relative to per-agent wallets and lowers gas costs for batched internal payments. Using historical DeFi liquidity data, we evaluate how reserve policies balance treasury returns against payment availability during market stress. We further examine the risks of automated bank runs and evaluate mechanisms to mitigate them.

papers.title: A Star is Reborn: The PHP Interpreter Rewritten in Safe Rust
papers.summary: PHP powers most of the web, yet its C interpreter has had many memory-safety vulnerabilities. Reimplementing the interpreter in safe Rust offers a promising way to eliminate these vulnerabilities. However, eliminating native memory violations alone does not necessarily prevent unintended accesses to the logical memory of the translated program. To prevent such failures, we introduce logical memory safety, which confines the program operations to their permitted memory. In this paper, we formalize this property for PHP through an abstract PHP machine model that captures how the PHP interpreter manages program values while abstracting away functionality details. Guided by this model, we reimplement the PHP 5.0.0 engine in safe Rust, and formally prove that, for a core fragment of PHP, our Rust translation refines the abstract PHP machine, thereby establishing logical memory safety for this fragment. Our translation safely handles all 173 memory vulnerabilities we collected that affect PHP 5.0.0 prior to the rewrite. The Rust version matches the C implementation on all functionality tests, and produces identical outputs for the real-world PHP applications we evaluate. To our knowledge, this is the first principled safe Rust port of a core fragment of the PHP interpreter that combines formal guarantees of logical memory safety with functional compatibility. The improved security comes at a modest average runtime overhead of only 15% compared to C.

papers.title: Analyzing Single-Bit Flips on LLMs and Their Backbone-Matched VLMs
papers.summary: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) enable offline weight analysis and are reused as backbones in vision-language models (VLMs), increasing the risk of bit-flip attacks that manipulate stored weight bits to induce malicious model behavior. An adversary could identify vulnerable bits on a public LLM and later flip the same locations in a deployed LLM or its backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip is particularly practical in this setting because it is easier to achieve under hardware fault attacks than multi-bit flips. However, existing selectors are mostly limited to multi-bit flips, without in-depth analysis of single-bit flips. In this paper, we adapt representative data-free and data-based bit selectors to identify candidate bits. We evaluate each bit independently on source LLMs and at the same logical coordinates in backbone-matched VLMs (without re-search), considering both performance degradation and prediction patterns across multiple inputs. Results show impact of single-bit flips varies across selectors on LLMs and their backbone-matched VLMs. A single-bit flip can make the model tend to produce a repeated output string across different inputs. Our robustness analysis reveals vulnerabilities in terms of performance and prediction patterns.
papers.title_zh: 分析大型语言模型及其骨干匹配视觉语言模型上的单比特翻转
papers.abstract_zh: 开放权重的大型语言模型（LLMs）支持离线权重分析，并被复用为视觉语言模型（VLMs）的骨干，这增加了比特翻转攻击的风险，此类攻击通过操纵存储的权重比特来诱导恶意模型行为。攻击者可以在公开的LLM上识别出脆弱比特，随后在已部署的LLM或其骨干匹配的VLMs中翻转相同位置的比特。在此场景下，单比特翻转尤其具有实际可行性，因为相比多比特翻转，它更容易在硬件故障攻击下实现。然而，现有选择器大多局限于多比特翻转，缺乏对单比特翻转的深入分析。本文中，我们改造了具有代表性的无数据比特选择器和基于数据的比特选择器来识别候选比特。我们在源LLMs上以及骨干匹配的VLMs中相同的逻辑坐标处（无需重新搜索）独立评估每个比特，同时考虑性能退化以及跨多个输入的预测模式。结果表明，单比特翻转的影响在LLMs及其骨干匹配的VLMs上因选择器而异。单比特翻转可使模型倾向于在不同输入下产生重复的输出字符串。我们的鲁棒性分析揭示了在性能和预测模式方面的脆弱性。

papers.title: Privacy Disclosure Control Benchmark (PDC-Bench): How Faithfully Do LLMs Keep Privacy Constraints on In-Context Disclosure Granularity?
papers.summary: In LLM task execution, a constraint on the permitted disclosure granularity of personal attributes is sometimes imposed on the output. For example, if a person's private attribute is their location (San Francisco) and disclosure is permitted only at the country level, an output at the state level (California) violates the constraint. Detecting such violations requires capturing not only direct privacy leakage (San Francisco) but also semantic leakage (California). However, existing benchmarks cannot measure the degree of leakage with respect to a given semantic constraint such as the country-level limit. We therefore formalize disclosure control as a constraint on the permitted ceiling over the hierarchy of a knowledge graph. Building on this formulation, we construct PDC-Bench, a benchmark of 16,105 samples covering geography, age, race and ethnicity, and occupation. In our experiments applying PDC-Bench to eleven LLMs, 62% of the constraint violations were semantic leakage. We further found that semantic leakage depends less on the model than on the permitted disclosure granularity and the task's need for the private attribute; reliable auditing must therefore target semantic leakage together with these two factors. Data, prompts, and code are available at https://github.com/fuji1655/PDC-Bench.

papers.title: Power Side-Channel Evaluation using Multi-FPGA Systems
papers.summary: Complex out-of-order processors are difficult to evaluate for power side-channel leakage before tapeout. A single FPGA often lacks sufficient capacity, whereas conventional CAD-based analysis is too slow to support the large numbers of traces required by practical attacks. Multi-FPGA emulation provides greater capacity, but existing partitioning schemes are not security-aware and thus results in poor attack performance. This work presents Scissors, a security-aware multi-FPGA partitioning approach for pre-silicon power side-channel evaluation of complex out-of-order processors. Scissors uses side-channel vulnerability factor (SVF) analysis to identify signals correlated with the secret key. It then keeps strongly key-correlated signals confined to one FPGA partition (measured) while moving rest of the signals to the other FPGAs (support), improving the observability of the side-channel information. We evaluate Scissors through RTL simulations and physical measurements on a two-U200 FPGA testbed, using frequency-domain CPA with a Hamming-weight leakage model. RTL ablation shows that only 68-71 high-SVF signals dominate key recovery process. For a single-core processor (SingleBOOM), Scissors recovers the key with 12,000 traces, compared with 49,000 for the unpartitioned design and 43,000 for TritonPart, while improving correct-key correlation by $2.83\times$. For a quad-core processor (QuadBOOM), which exceeds the capacity of the CW340 single-FPGA platform, Scissors reduces the required traces from 111,000 to 66,000 and improves correlation by $1.48\times$ over TritonPart. Scissors also reduces QuadBOOM RTL-to-bitstream generation from 61 h 39 min to 6 h 40 min, a $9.25\times$ speedup. These results show that security-aware partitioning improves leakage observability and attack performance while substantially reducing implementation time for complex processors against the baseline method.

papers.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs) cause large language models (LLMs) to exhibit malicious behavior after quantization while remaining benign at high precision. Existing defenses often rely on security-guided configuration selection or iterative optimization, but do not identify which quantization-induced changes should be repaired. We isolate module-local quantization effects from upstream drift by evaluating the high-precision and quantized versions of each module on identical states from the quantized inference trajectory, and formulate QCB defense as repairing the resulting same-state operator discrepancies. We propose ReQOR, a training-free defense that identifies the dominant directions of these discrepancies on benign calibration data and restores the full-precision computation along them in closed form, yielding a factorized residual adapter. ReQOR uses neither attack information nor gradient-based optimization and supports both full-span and low-rank repair. Experiments across four LLMs, three PGD-based QCB attacks, three malicious behaviors, and three quantization formats show substantial QCB mitigation while largely preserving benign utility. In additional experiments on a non-PGD outlier-injection attack, existing baselines largely fail, whereas ReQOR remains effective. Further analysis shows that dominant operator-discrepancy directions provide more effective and rank-efficient repair than rank-matched random, low-energy, or raw weight-error directions, while low-rank ReQOR reduces deployment memory overhead.
papers.title_zh: ReQOR：面向大语言模型中量化条件后门的算子差异子空间修复
papers.abstract_zh: 量化条件后门（QCBs）会使大语言模型（LLMs）在量化后表现出恶意行为，而在高精度下仍保持良性。现有防御往往依赖安全引导的配置选择或迭代优化，但并未识别出哪些由量化引起的变化应当被修复。我们通过在每个模块的量化推理轨迹中取相同状态，分别评估该模块的高精度版本与量化版本，从而将模块局部的量化效应与上游漂移隔离开来，并将 QCB 防御表述为修复由此产生的同状态算子差异。我们提出 ReQOR，这是一种免训练的防御方法，它在良性校准数据上识别这些差异的主导方向，并以闭式解沿这些方向恢复全精度计算，从而得到一个因子化残差适配器。ReQOR 既不使用攻击信息，也不使用基于梯度的优化，并同时支持全跨度修复与低秩修复。在四种 LLMs、三种基于 PGD 的 QCB 攻击、三种恶意行为以及三种量化格式上的实验表明，ReQOR 能大幅缓解 QCB，同时基本保持良性效用。在针对一种非 PGD 的离群值注入攻击的额外实验中，现有基线大多失效，而 ReQOR 仍然有效。进一步分析表明，主导的算子差异方向所提供的修复比秩匹配的随机方向、低能量方向或原始权重误差方向更有效且秩效率更高，同时低秩 ReQOR 降低了部署内存开销。

papers.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
papers.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. In these systems, multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion are often viewed as robustness-enhancing mechanisms against content manipulation, as compression can filter noisy signals and cross-modal consensus can suppress inconsistent anomalies. We challenge this assumption by showing that the same process can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent support across modalities can gain disproportionate influence in candidate comparison, offering an exploitable direction for content manipulation. In this paper, we introduce C3H, a novel inference-time attack that exploits this vulnerability. Rather than relying on noisy perturbations or training-time poisoning, C3H promotes a target item by tailoring its multimodal content to align with the decision criteria implicitly expressed by the recommender. Extensive experiments demonstrate that C3H substantially increases target-item exposure while maintaining overall recommendation utility. Code is available at https://github.com/GuoweiGuan666/C3H.
papers.title_zh: C3H：多模态大语言模型推荐系统中的压缩到共识准则劫持
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）正在将推荐系统转变为内容感知的决策系统。在这些系统中，多模态压缩与跨模态融合常被视为增强鲁棒性、抵御内容操纵的机制，因为压缩可以过滤噪声信号，而跨模态共识可以抑制不一致的异常。我们对这一假设提出挑战，证明同一过程会在排序决策中暴露出一种压缩到共识（C2C）偏差。在压缩后仍然显著、并在各模态间获得一致支持的信号，可以在候选比较中获得不成比例的影响力，从而为内容操纵提供了一个可利用的方向。本文提出 C3H，一种利用该漏洞的新型推理时攻击。C3H 不依赖噪声扰动或训练时投毒，而是通过定制目标项的多模态内容，使其与推荐器隐式表达出的决策准则相一致，从而提升目标项。大量实验表明，C3H 在保持整体推荐效用的同时显著提高了目标项的曝光度。代码可在 https://github.com/GuoweiGuan666/C3H 获取。

papers.title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
papers.summary: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers. Since real costs are not public, we measure on synthetic firms with known values how much an honest-but-curious provider recovers when it knows the disguise algorithm, holds sector-level price and margin statistics, and links a firm's queries. In one prompt, per-field scaling, a fixed-axis instantiation of Zhang et al.'s order-preserving substitution and Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt's released sanitizer keep the attacker's margin-hit advantage over a prior-only guess between -0.6 and +4.4 percentage points. After 16 linked queries with fresh secrets, every disguise we test (Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon\geq 0.5$) has a target recovered significantly more often: under the order-preserving substitution, margin recovery rises from 25.0% to 59.4%. The same attacker recovers 29.4 percentage points more margins with fresh maps than with one reused map. Theory explains the contrast: one reused secret bounds all queries by a single full-precision view of the fields shown, whereas fresh scaling keys are identifiable. Except for Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon=0.5$, the gains persist when the attacker's prior comes from another population model and when values drift by up to 5% between queries; on our firms, whose prose cues are weak, reading the prose with a language model adds at most 2.5 points. Code and data: https://github.com/Jamli58/fresh-keys-stale-secrets

papers.title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents
papers.summary: AI agents are beginning to automate data analysis, orchestration, and simulation steering in HPC environments, but they introduce a security problem that existing cluster defenses do not address: the hijacked authorized agent. An adversary can subvert an agent through prompt injection, poisoned shared data, compromised tools, or multi-agent coordination, then exfiltrate sensitive data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic. We propose behavioral attestation as a runtime defense for this setting. Our system, AEGIS, compiles task-derived behavioral constraints, monitors agent actions with ebpf-based syscall interception, verifies evidence against constraint profiles, correlates behavior across agents, and triggers slurm-level containment. On the real attestation path, AEGIS detects all four implemented attack classes with sub-second median latency at a 1-second interval and low measured verifier overhead. Controlled experiments show full attack-suite coverage, stronger detection than representative baselines, and no observed false positives on the evaluated benign workflows.

papers.title: PORTA: Systematic Discovery of Vulnerabilities in Identity Brokers
papers.summary: Identity brokers such as Keycloak, Vault, and Dex translate authentication proofs from an upstream identity provider into sessions for downstream services. Due to their central role in authentication and trust mediation, a single vulnerability in a broker compromises every downstream service behind it. In fact, recent incidents have demonstrated that even widely adopted platforms are not immune to such issues, highlighting the critical need for systematic analysis. To build such an analysis, this work first defines invariants for broker operation. These invariants are not completely covered by existing authentication specifications, primarily because brokers are unique in their duality, i.e., acting simultaneously as a relying party and an identity provider. The invariants capture the properties that identity brokers must uphold throughout their workflows, as all 60 previous CVEs we consider violate at least one invariant. Within these workflows, we further define high-level action categories. Equipped with this information, our automated tool PORTA leverages a large language model (LLM) to generate API invocation sequences corresponding to the high-level action categories, and oracle assertions aligned with the specified invariants. PORTA identifies 33 previously unreported security vulnerabilities in seven popular open-source brokers. We study these novel vulnerabilities and trace them to eight recurring patterns. We responsibly disclosed all discovered vulnerabilities: 29 have been confirmed, 14 patched, and 19 assigned CVE numbers, with 10 CVEs rated as critical.
papers.title_zh: PORTA：身份代理中漏洞的系统化发现
papers.abstract_zh: Keycloak、Vault 和 Dex 等身份代理将来自上游身份提供方的认证证明转换为面向下游服务的会话。由于它们在认证和信任中介中的核心作用，代理中的单个漏洞就会危及位于其后的每一个下游服务。事实上，近期事件已经表明，即使是广泛采用的平台也不能免受此类问题的影响，这凸显了系统性分析的迫切需求。为构建这样的分析，本文首先定义代理运行的不变式。这些不变式并未被现有认证规范完全覆盖，主要是因为代理在其双重性上具有独特性，即同时充当依赖方和身份提供方。这些不变式刻画了身份代理在其整个工作流中必须保持的性质，因为我们考虑的此前全部 60 个 CVE 都违反了至少一个不变式。在这些工作流内，我们进一步定义了高层动作类别。借助这些信息，我们的自动化工具 PORTA 利用大型语言模型（LLM）生成与高层动作类别相对应的 API 调用序列，以及与所指定不变式一致的 oracle 断言。PORTA 在七个流行的开源代理中识别出 33 个此前未报告的安全漏洞。我们研究了这些新颖漏洞，并将其追溯到八种反复出现的模式。我们负责任地披露了所有已发现的漏洞：29 个已确认，14 个已修补，19 个已分配 CVE 编号，其中 10 个 CVE 被评为严重。

papers.title: A Bernstein-Type Variance-Adaptive PMW Mechanism for DP Query Release
papers.summary: Private Multiplicative Weights (PMW) is a central mechanism for the differentially private release of adaptive linear statistics over a finite universe. Its classical analysis uses a fixed multiplicative-weights learning rate and does not exploit the local variance of the current hypothesis. This paper presents PMW-Bernstein, a variance-adaptive refinement in which the update step is determined by the relationship between the privately estimated query error and the variance under the current hypothesis. The mechanism retains the standard PMW privacy architecture based on Sparse Vector screening, Gaussian numerical measurements, sequential composition, and post-processing. Through a potential-based analysis, we prove a one-step progress bound that yields a global weighted energy bound, recovers the classical $O(1/α2)$ update regime in general, and establishes an $O(1/α)$ update regime under a Bernsteintype condition on updated rounds. Controlled simulations over synthetic finite-universe distributions and query workloads show that the adaptive rule reduces the number of updates in the low-variance regime, remains competitive in the high-variance regime, and succeeds within the prescribed update budget in the heterogeneous regime where the fixed-step baseline fails.

papers.title: CoRe: Jointly Learning Contextual Representations for Understanding and Generation
papers.summary: We introduce CoRe, in which understanding and generation jointly shape one contextual representation for images and one for text, trained from scratch. Each representation is read for understanding, conditions the other modality, and is the space in which that modality is generated by a continuous flow from Gaussian noise. With 383M parameters trained on CC12M and no pretrained language model, text encoder, or VAE at inference, CoRe matches a same-data contrastive-only baseline in global understanding and reaches COCO-30K FID 10.10, comparable to much larger generators built on pretrained components. In controlled comparisons at equal data and architecture, CoRe generates better in both directions (text to image and image to text) than a representation shaped by understanding alone and then frozen, and follows prompts better than generating in a space that understanding does not shape. In the other direction, with an attentive segmentation probe, on monocular depth, and when read by a frozen language model, CoRe surpasses the contrastive-only baseline: generation adds information that stronger readouts reach. Because generation runs inside the understanding representation, frozen real-image probes read and steer intermediate states and the model ranks its own samples without extra training. Because both modalities use continuous flows, both also distill to a few steps. Our controls indicate why one representation suffices: understanding organizes the representation semantically, while generation makes it retain more information.

papers.title: A dataset of clinically similar image pairs from citation-linked case reports for medical image retrieval
papers.summary: Retrieving images of patients clinically similar to a given patient can support diagnosis, teaching and research. Training and evaluating retrieval systems requires knowing which images of different patients show the same finding, and existing datasets are small or narrow in scope. We construct PMC-PaIR, a dataset of 86,144 pairs of clinically similar images from 56,013 open-access PubMed Central case reports, which often document rare or challenging presentations. We develop an approach that follows citations, which often link case reports of similar patients. To determine what two linked cases share clinically, it prompts large language models to generate and answer hierarchical questions, from modality to diagnosis and findings, and to match images by caption using the answers. Experts find the pairs highly accurate, and this question-guided approach finds twice as many correct pairs as direct matching. Fine-tuning BiomedCLIP on PMC-PaIR improves retrieval in all modality, anatomy and diagnosis categories tested, for image-only queries and image queries with a short text naming the finding. We release the dataset and the automated pipeline, which can extend PMC-PaIR as new case reports are published.
papers.title_zh: 用于医学图像检索的、来自引文关联病例报告的临床相似图像对数据集
papers.abstract_zh: 检索与给定患者在临床上相似的患者图像可以支持诊断、教学和研究。训练和评估检索系统需要知道不同患者的哪些图像显示了相同的发现，而现有数据集规模较小或范围狭窄。我们构建了 PMC-PaIR，这是一个包含来自 56,013 篇开放获取 PubMed Central 病例报告的 86,144 对临床相似图像的数据集，这些病例报告通常记录了罕见或具有挑战性的临床表现。我们开发了一种沿着引文追踪的方法，引文常常将相似患者的病例报告联系起来。为了确定两个相关联的病例在临床上共享什么，该方法提示大语言模型生成并回答从成像模态到诊断和发现的层级式问题，并利用这些答案通过图注来匹配图像。专家发现这些图像对具有很高的准确性，而且这种问题引导的方法找到的正确图像对数量是直接匹配方法的两倍。在 PMC-PaIR 上微调 BiomedCLIP 可在所测试的所有模态、解剖结构和诊断类别中改善检索，无论是以纯图像查询，还是以图像加上一段指明发现的简短文本进行查询。我们发布了该数据集和自动化流程，随着新的病例报告发表，该流程可以扩展 PMC-PaIR。

papers.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
papers.summary: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. Code, models, and data are released.

papers.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing
papers.summary: Real editing requests describe a look, not the steps to reach it, so an agent that serves them must judge how much of each tool the look takes. Existing benchmarks do not measure this: their tasks either state the tools and values, or leave the amount open and are scored by VLM judges that pass more than half of half- and triple-strength results. We introduce GoldiBench, a benchmark of 500 editing tasks in five professional applications (darktable, RawTherapee, GIMP, Inkscape, Blender), solvable by writing a program or by operating the GUI. Each task pairs a START image with a TARGET rendered from a hidden program, so the amount is fixed by a known target; the agent's edit is re-rendered and compared with TARGET, and the same task is posed with the tools and values, the tools only, or the goal only, separating operation from effect judgement. Across 25 open, GUI and closed models, agents operate well (99-100% with programs from 4B up when told the values) but fall off a cliff when they must judge the amount: given only the tools, the best model passes 19% of the tasks with programs and 33% through the GUI, and scale does not close the gap. Manuals barely help; the measured TARGET-START difference more than doubles the pass rate, but the same difference shown as an image does not for open models. Allowed four renders, agents almost always stop after the first; forced to compare, the strong models double their pass rate. Agents know the tools, but neither read nor check the amount.

papers.title: RePT: 3D Geometry Emerges from 2D Relational Pretraining
papers.summary: Learning spatial representations often relies on explicitly predicting geometric quantities, but how physical geometry is organized within learned representations remains less understood. We ask whether 3D structure can emerge from learning relations across 2D observations, without 3D prediction targets. We introduce RePT, which learns compact relations between distinct physical points through cross-view 2D point prediction. The learned relation space develops a geometric organization in which magnitudes, angles, and neighborhoods reflect physical 3D displacement. A single linear readout fitted on 16 scenes recovers displacement length and angle on 39 held-out scenes without refitting (Pearson r = 0.72 and 0.78). The ARKitScenes-trained checkpoint also retains strong geometric organization on ScanNet++, showcasing generalizability. In controlled comparisons, distinct-point relational prediction consistently yields stronger geometric organization than matched same-point correspondence learning. This organization depends on additive relations and adaptive scene context, and higher point-transfer accuracy does not by itself produce stronger organization. More broadly, our results suggest that 3D geometry need not be an explicit prediction target and can instead emerge as a structural property of representations trained to relate 2D observations, pointing to relational prediction as a complementary route to learning the representations that spatial intelligence builds on.

papers.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions
papers.summary: Concept-based models justify a decision by concepts they claim to see, decoded through an explicit ontology. Yet concept predictions are known to leak label information, ignore locality, and be poorly grounded on new attribute combinations. A decision decoded from such concepts can satisfy the ontology and still be wrong, so we ask when it can serve as a certificate. On unseen combinations of familiar parts, a joint concept bottleneck model and a concept embedding model, trained as is standard, certify wrong classes 93-94% of the time despite a correct ontology (60% for a joint model trained only on visible parts and gated by a localizer). The joint model's part errors copy co-occurring values more often than chance (cross-concept shortcutting). Treating the ontology as an error-detecting code, we show that a certificate needs visible evidence excluding every rival, unseen parts reported as such, and rare misreads not driven by a shared shortcut. A minimal reference design, OCVE, reads each part from a local crop in its own forward pass. On unseen FunnyBirds classes, it certifies 52% of images at 0.4% risk, against 14% for mask-pooled features and 33% for full-image part readers (5.6% when trained and gated alike), at similar zero-shot accuracy. The best baselines, even calibrated or restricted to unseen classes, and a decoder counting only agreeing parts remain about 3-8 times riskier. On CUB, isolated region readers are more accurate than an attribute-prototype model (63.1% vs. 55.3%) and certify unseen species at about 6 points less risk than it and about 10 points less than features pooled in the same keypoint boxes. On real traffic signs, isolated readers lower certified risk from 99.8% to 67%, which is still far too high; most remaining errors are misread pictograms. On seen classes the ontology brings no gain over a fairly trained black box, and isolation costs accuracy.

papers.title: Anchoring VAE Fine-Tuning to Its Latent Diffusion Prior
papers.summary: Pretrained latent diffusion models are effective priors for transfer learning, from geometry estimation to physics simulation. Existing approaches fine-tune the diffusion backbone but freeze the encoder of the VAE to preserve the latent distribution. However, a frozen encoder may miss salient details in non-RGB inputs and is limited to three channels. We introduce Diffusion Prior Anchoring (DPA), a regularizer applied during VAE fine-tuning that uses a score-distillation update to steer latents toward the high-density manifold on which the pretrained diffusion model denoises accurately. We validate DPA across three image and video models (FLUX 3, LTX-Video, Wan2.2) and four tasks: monocular depth estimation, MRI reconstruction, wind-flow simulation, and surface normal estimation, where DPA lowers the prediction error by 7.5% relative to the frozen VAE, 4.9% to decoder-only fine-tuning, and 4.0% to unanchored VAE fine-tuning. Its gain grows the further the target data lies from the RGB training distribution, from 3.3% on monocular depth estimation to 7.2% on complex-valued MRI. DPA also applies to modified VAEs, including pruned and multi-channel variants. With a four-channel VAE that encodes depth and surface normals, it lowers depth estimation error by 9.3%.
papers.title_zh: 将 VAE 微调锚定到其潜在扩散先验
papers.abstract_zh: 预训练的潜在扩散模型是迁移学习的有效先验，涵盖从几何估计到物理模拟的任务。现有方法微调扩散主干网络，但冻结 VAE 的编码器以保持潜在分布。然而，冻结的编码器可能会遗漏非 RGB 输入中的显著细节，并且受限于三个通道。我们提出扩散先验锚定（Diffusion Prior Anchoring, DPA），这是一种在 VAE 微调期间应用的正则化器，它使用分数蒸馏更新将潜在变量引导至预训练扩散模型能够准确去噪的高密度流形。我们在三个图像与视频模型（FLUX 3、LTX-Video、Wan2.2）和四个任务上验证了 DPA：单目深度估计、MRI 重建、风流模拟和表面法线估计，其中 DPA 相对于冻结 VAE 将预测误差降低了 7.5%，相对于仅解码器微调降低了 4.9%，相对于无锚定 VAE 微调降低了 4.0%。当目标数据距离 RGB 训练分布越远时，其增益越大，从单目深度估计上的 3.3% 增至复值 MRI 上的 7.2%。DPA 也适用于修改后的 VAE，包括剪枝和多通道变体。在使用编码深度和表面法线的四通道 VAE 时，它将深度估计误差降低了 9.3%。

papers.title: A Piecewise-Linear Activation Function for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.summary: Coordinate networks with ReLU activations perform poorly on implicit neural representation tasks, and the activations that address this, such as sinusoids and Gabor wavelets, all leave the piecewise-linear function class, so it remains unclear which property of ReLU is at fault. We introduce JaSIN, a family of bounded piecewise-linear activations that interpolates between ReLU and a piecewise-linear sinusoid without any the use of transcendental operation. Our results show that a bounded range improves image reconstruction PSNR on average by 0.06 dB, a single bump 3.29 dB, and centering that bump a further 3.64 dB. The oscillation count improves 6.30 dB more, raising ReLU from 24.0 to 37.3 dB on Kodak images, placing third over eleven activations, within 1.3 dB of the state-of-the-art, though beyond four oscillations the reconstruction collapses. Because an INR is fit on the grid on which it is evaluated, a unit whose pre-activations never reach the support of its activation is certifiably inactive over the entire domain; deleting such units is lossless without fine-tuning, removing up to 84% of parameters at zero loss in performance (dB) and decoding 3.2 times faster. Reference code and demos are available at https://github.com/jeovafarias/jasin.

papers.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration
papers.summary: Image restoration remains a fundamental challenge in low-level vision, requiring methods that handle diverse degradations while preserving scene structures and details. We revisit classical Retinex theory and propose a Generalized Retinex formulation that extends the illumination-reflectance decomposition into a Retinex-inspired content-environment factorization prior for image restoration. The key idea is to restore images using two learned factors: a content-dominant response (generalized reflectance) capturing scene properties and an environment-side response (generalized illumination) encoding task-dependent variations associated with the observed degradations. Based on this formulation, we develop GRUN (Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network), a MAP-guided deep unfolding framework that alternates reflectance restoration, illumination estimation, and progressive degradation inference across K stages with degradation-conditioned proximal operators. We further introduce a Degradation-aware Coupling Regularizer (DCR) that combines mutual information minimization, gradient decorrelation, and scale anchoring to promote complementary content-environment factor representations. Experiments on seven image restoration tasks, including denoising, dehazing, deraining, low-light enhancement, deblurring, underwater enhancement, and backlit enhancement, demonstrate competitive results on multiple benchmarks using the same architecture with task-specific weights. Moreover, the proposed Generalized Retinex design can be integrated into existing restoration methods, demonstrating its cross-architecture applicability. Code will be released.

papers.title: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation
papers.summary: Event cameras report asynchronous brightness changes, yet metric-depth supervision is typically available only at sparsely sampled reference timestamps. Aggregating events into frame-like representations simplifies learning but can obscure the fine-grained temporal structure of the original event stream. We introduce EventSSM, a causal spatial-state framework for event-associated metric-depth estimation using a recurrent memory updated by chronological event packets. To bridge asynchronous predictions and frame-time supervision, predicted event depths are geometrically transported using calibrated camera poses and differentiably rendered at reference timestamps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate improvements over established event-depth methods across multiple depth-error measures. Controlled ablations further examine cross-modal initialization, temporal recurrence, individual state, readout, and supervision components, and packet subdivision. Together, these findings establish EventSSM as an effective framework for causal event-associated metric-depth estimation, combining persistent spatial context with physically timed state retention.

papers.title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation
papers.summary: Understanding a group conversation means deciding, from video and audio, who is speaking and to whom. Leading systems treat these tasks offline on single-channel clips and align models with a self-evaluation reward. We propose BEARING, a geometry-first alternative built on one measured signal: the direction from which a microphone array beside the camera hears a sound. A label-free calibration learned from the stream registers this direction into the camera image, and an online registry of faces, voices and directions needs no enrollment. The registered direction serves as (i) a visual prompt for a vision-language model, a marker on the speaker or an arrow toward an off-screen source; (ii) one input of a reliability-weighted fusion with visual active-speaker detection, for speakers in the same direction from the array; and (iii) a verifiable reward for alignment: the named speaker must sit where the sound comes from, the confidence must match that check, and always answering "group" earns nothing. Every decision is online, with the lookahead as an explicit parameter. On 9,498 addressee-labelled utterances from three AMI sites and egocentric EasyCom, the direction prompt raises speaker accuracy from 54% to 74%; addressee accuracy moves by about two points, because telling one addressee from the group depends on the words more than on where people are. For co-located speakers on AVDIAR, visual active-speaker detection holds 95% where direction alone falls to 59%. The verifiable reward beats self-evaluation under GRPO, reward-ranked fine-tuning and DPO; shrinking the lookahead from 5 s to 0.5 s costs 4.5 DER points on AMI, and learning the registration online costs a dip in the first two minutes before the system overtakes vision alone. Code and evaluation protocols will be released.

papers.title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
papers.summary: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined. These procedures make up for the weaknesses of older models by keeping them on a task-specific path, but with frontier models that reliably plan and use tools, they can lower accuracy. We propose RVLM-X, a task-generalizable recursive VLM harness that runs unchanged across photographs, charts and maps. Following the recursive inference of Recursive Language Models, the VLM programmatically controls its own visual context in a code REPL that holds the full-resolution image and calls itself recursively on regions that it chooses. With a cost-efficient frontier model as the base of every method, RVLM-X is more accurate than a single call on all 7 public benchmarks and has the highest pooled accuracy. Because existing benchmarks mostly test whether a model finds one small detail, we also introduce MapGenBench, procedurally generated maps whose questions combine fine-detail perception with multi-step reasoning. There, RVLM-X answers 71.4% of held-out questions against 55.5% for the strongest baseline. Overall, our findings suggest that as VLMs plan and use tools more reliably, letting the model write its own visual search works better than fixing one in advance.

papers.title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
papers.summary: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization. We introduce RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild, text-paired dataset of ~542K sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps) which is an order of magnitude larger than prior work. To ensure high-quality supervision, a stringent dexterity filter discards low-articulation sequences, focusing the distribution on complex bimanual movement. Each clip is paired with five captions at increasing granularities from global semantic tags to atomic finger states, organized under a hierarchical taxonomy. To bridge the gap between body and hand architectures, we propose a novel 393-D bimanual representation that adapts redundant body-motion paradigms to the high-DoF kinematics of hands. Systematic benchmarking of diffusion, masked-token, and autoregressive generators reveals distinct trade-offs under these hand-specific adaptations, including a sharp divergence between semantic alignment and kinematic plausibility. Our dataset, representation, and benchmark establish a rigorous foundation for the next generation of dexterous motion synthesis. Project page: https://romodataset.github.io/romo-hands/.
papers.title_zh: RoMo Hands：一个大规模、组织丰富的文本到手部运动数据集
papers.abstract_zh: 尽管文本驱动的身体运动生成已趋于成熟，纯手部的合成仍受制于数据瓶颈。现有数据集往往将手视为刚性的末端执行器、缺乏细粒度的描述文本，或在规模上过于有限而无法支撑稳健的泛化。我们提出 RoMo Hands，这是一个面向真实场景（in-the-wild）、与文本配对的数据集，包含约 542K 条序列（884 小时，30 fps 下 95.5M 帧），规模比先前工作大一个数量级。为确保高质量的监督，一个严格的灵巧度过滤器会剔除关节活动度低的序列，使数据分布聚焦于复杂的双手运动。每个片段都配有五条描述文本，其粒度由全局语义标签递增至原子级手指状态，并组织在一个层级化分类体系之下。为弥合身体架构与手部架构之间的差距，我们提出一种新颖的 393 维双手表示，将冗余的身体运动范式适配到手部的高自由度运动学。对扩散模型、掩码 token 模型与自回归生成器的系统性基准测试揭示了在这些面向手部的适配下各自不同的权衡，包括语义对齐与运动学合理性之间的显著分歧。我们的数据集、表示方法与基准测试为下一代灵巧运动合成奠定了严谨的基础。项目主页：https://romodataset.github.io/romo-hands/。

papers.title: BODYBENCH: Evaluating Adversarial Image Defenses Against AI Nudification Inpainting
papers.summary: Adversarial perturbation defenses protect images from unauthorized edits by adding imperceptible noise. Yet none of these methods have been evaluated against nudification, despite AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery (AIG-NCII) being among the most documented harms of generative AI. Moreover, nudification edits are readily carried out through inpainting, the primary setting these protection methods are designed to defend against. We argue this is a problem-formulation failure since prior threat models do not correspond to nudification edits (also called attacks). The misalignment of existing approaches is structural, spanning mask shape, training and testing prompt distributions, and success criterion which causes existing evaluations to systematically overestimate protection effectiveness. We reformulate image protection against unauthorized editing around this documented harm. We introduce BODYBENCH, a benchmark of 648 fully synthetic clothed adult subjects, each paired with 11 mask variants spanning body, face, and context regions. We propose three harm-aligned metrics: sexualization, naturalness, and recognizability that jointly determine whether an inpainted output constitutes a successful nudification attack. Auditing four recent protection methods (PhotoGuard, DiffusionGuard, AdvPaint, DiffVax) on BODYBENCH, we find that protection succeeds in only one configuration of one method, and only under exact mask alignment between defender and attacker---a condition no real defender can guarantee and one that we show is easily always bypassed. We also show that standard evaluation metrics such as peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) are essentially uncorrelated with nudification protection. BODYBENCH makes this misalignment measurable and provides a foundation for defenses grounded in documented harm.
papers.title_zh: BODYBENCH：评估对抗性图像防御对 AI 裸体化修复的抵御效果
papers.abstract_zh: 对抗性扰动防御通过添加不可感知的噪声来保护图像免受未经授权的编辑。然而，这些方法均尚未针对裸体化进行过评估，尽管 AI 生成的未经同意的私密影像（AIG-NCII）是生成式 AI 最有据可查的危害之一。此外，裸体化编辑很容易通过图像修复实现，而图像修复正是这些保护方法旨在防御的主要场景。我们认为这是问题形式化上的失败，因为先前的威胁模型并不对应于裸体化编辑（也称为攻击）。现有方法的错位是结构性的，涵盖掩码形状、训练与测试提示分布以及成功判据，这导致现有评估系统性地高估保护有效性。我们围绕这一有据可查的危害，重新形式化针对未经授权编辑的图像保护问题。我们引入 BODYBENCH，一个包含 648 名完全合成的、穿着衣服的成年受试者的基准，每名受试者都配有 11 个掩码变体，涵盖身体、面部和上下文区域。我们提出三个与危害对齐的指标：性化程度、自然度和可识别性，它们共同决定修复后的输出是否构成一次成功的裸体化攻击。在 BODYBENCH 上审计四种近期保护方法（PhotoGuard、DiffusionGuard、AdvPaint、DiffVax）后，我们发现保护仅在一种方法的一种配置下成功，并且仅在防御者与攻击者之间掩码精确对齐的条件下成功——这是任何真实防御者都无法保证的条件，而且我们证明该条件很容易被始终绕过。我们还表明，诸如峰值信噪比（PSNR）之类的标准评估指标与裸体化保护基本上不相关。BODYBENCH 使这种错位变得可测量，并为以有据可查的危害为基础的防御提供了基础。

papers.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
papers.summary: Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy. However, existing works have two limitations: 1) TSFMs reduce the predictive distribution to its median or mean, flattening diverse futures into a calm line, and 2) multimodal TS forecasting models incorporate text into the forecaster through TS-language alignment, which is substantially weaker than vision-language alignment. To address these limitations, we propose the VIsion-language SelectOR (VISOR), a multimodal TS forecasting framework that selects one plausible future instead of averaging across candidates, leveraging the alignment capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to select the most suitable candidate based on textual information. VISOR consists of two components: 1) a text-free stochastic predictor that samples diverse candidate futures, and 2) a VLM selector that reads the candidates as a single chart image and selects one based on the text. To avoid overly calm forecasting paths, we train the selector with a shape-aware target that evaluates each candidate based on both point-wise error and path shape. Across three benchmarks covering ten datasets, VISOR achieves the best average ranking in both point and volatility errors compared with TSFMs and multimodal TS forecasting models. Code: https://github.com/seunghan96/VISOR.

papers.title: Gaze World Model
papers.summary: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improves both shift detection and gaze localization. Given a video clip and the person's head box, GWM estimates gaze locations and detects gaze shifts in the observed clip, and forecasts future gaze and shifts from predicted scene features. To train and evaluate these tasks, we augment VideoAttentionTarget and ChildPlay with event-level gaze-shift annotations. GWM achieves state-of-the-art shift detection on these benchmarks, about 10 points higher in four-class AP than the strongest baseline, while remaining comparable to the strongest image-based models in gaze target estimation, and outperforms the compared baselines on future gaze localization and shift forecasting.

papers.title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
papers.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it. We call this the context shortcut. Conditioning the predictor on the radiology report repairs the prediction, but in our setup the encoder gains little over image-only pretraining: the report supplies what the encoder never had to learn. JECT therefore gives the report two roles: a condition for the predictor and, through masked section-text prediction, a target for the encoder, which must predict the report's anatomical sections from the unmasked scan. A hierarchical three-dimensional encoder that predicts at every stage keeps this clinical content at every scale. In ablations, the text target improves classification and localization, while conditioning adds little to the encoder. Trained from scratch on 173k volumes, the recipe reaches the level of current computed tomography foundation models in classification, retrieval and nodule malignancy, and of task-specific models in lung-cancer risk prediction after fine-tuning. Conditioning still matters: its predictor can be reused, with no extra training, to show where a report sentence acts, changing most at the finding the sentence describes. Code and pretrained weights are available.

papers.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
papers.summary: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configuration, and analyze performance and interaction trajectories across models and tasks. Adaptive observation yields substantial gains on fine-grained action understanding, with benefits also extending to Video-MME-v2. Even under the same observation interface, gains differ substantially across models; interaction traces reveal corresponding differences in evidence seeking and the reliability of answer revision. The benefits also vary across tasks for the same model, ranging from substantial improvements to limited gains and regressions. Together, these findings support an account in which harness effectiveness depends on the alignment between opportunities for informative observation and the model's ability to turn interaction into reliable revisions. They motivate video harnesses that coordinate perception and reasoning, matching observational autonomy to task demands and model capabilities.

papers.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
papers.summary: Knowledge-intensive video generation remains challenging because prompts often omit the facts, appearances, and temporal relationships required for accurate generation. While search-based workflows can retrieve missing evidence, manually designed strategies limit adaptive planning, and conventional training suffers from costly video-level feedback and coarse trajectory-level credit assignment. In this paper, we present Loupe, a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to construct evidence-grounded temporal video prompts with reference images. We further introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), which leverages prompt-specific factual, visual, and temporal requirements to evaluate intermediate search and planning decisions before video rendering. Building on RBC, RBC-SFT reweights assistant-token learning by step quality, while RBC-GRPO incorporates step-level credits alongside a final planning reward, without rendering videos during RL. To address the lack of dedicated search-oriented evaluation, we construct Search-VBench, which contains 150 held-out prompts across seven categories. Experiments show that Loupe improves all four evaluation dimensions across three video generators, raising the overall score of MiniMax-H3 from 32.80 to 70.67 and outperforming an untrained search workflow. Ablation experiments show that full RBC training outperforms standard SFT followed by trajectory-level GRPO by 5.27 points. Human evaluations and results on Sci-VBench and KIVI-Bench further demonstrate improved generation quality, scientific grounding, factual precision, and helpfulness. Our project page is available at https://zengkaiya.github.io/Loupe/.

papers.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
papers.summary: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed to assess emerging hypotheses. Their spatial attention guides view placement, contextual responses determine crop extent, and observation history encourages complementary inspection. The resulting predictions are combined through uncertainty-weighted voting. On ScreenSpot-Pro, SPARK improves grounding accuracy over single-view inference by 13.9, 25.2, and 16.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, and UI-TARS, outperforming all compared test-time methods for each backbone. Consistent gains across four additional benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse interfaces and grounding tasks. These results establish semantic probing as an effective mechanism for turning a frozen VLM's understanding of what to inspect into more accurate GUI grounding.

papers.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
papers.summary: Hands grasp objects with soft skin. A fingertip flattens against a mug, and a palm curves around a bottle. Yet hand-object datasets and estimators represent the hand as a rigid articulated mesh, which hovers above or penetrates the object where skin would press against it. Existing refiners keep the mesh rigid and adjust only the pose, trading pose accuracy for physical plausibility. We ask whether a rigid hand can instead touch the object as skin does while staying close to its original pose. We lift annotated or estimated rigid hands to contact-consistent meshes through an optimization that (i) slightly adjusts the joints and wrist to bring the fingers onto the object, (ii) deforms the skin so that penetrating regions settle onto the surface, and (iii) keeps this deformation consistent over time. Since deformation reaches only skin already near the object, we further train a lightweight head on the lifted annotations to predict where an estimated hand should touch and steer the deformation there. Unlike existing refiners, the lift more than doubles the skin lying on the object surface for three published estimators while barely changing the pose. Guidance from the learned head further improves grasp stability by closing contact gaps that the estimate leaves open. Existing hand-object datasets and estimators can thus adopt contact-consistent hands without changing the hand model or retraining the estimators.

papers.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
papers.summary: Looped transformers reuse one block of shared weights along the depth of the network. Recent looped diffusion transformers are trained from scratch, which repeats the full pretraining cost although strong pretrained non-looped diffusion transformers exist. We propose Distill to Loop (Dooop), which distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student whose blocks are initialized from the teacher's. We cast distillation as a fixed-point iteration toward the teacher, in which the output after every loop is trained toward the teacher, and each loop is one step of an ordinary differential equation in depth. As a result, one model runs any number of loops at test time without retraining, and the higher-order ODE solvers of diffusion model sampling can be applied along the depth dimension for better results. Meanwhile, because a looped model produces an output after every loop, we also construct loop guidance between the outputs of different loop counts, which improves the generated samples at little extra compute. On SD3-medium, a looped student with about 37% of the teacher's parameters matches the teacher on average over GenEval, ImageReward, PickScore and HPSv2.1 with two to four loops, and with two loops it uses about 58% of the teacher's compute. And on a four-step SD3-medium, loop guidance raises the average of the four metrics from 88.2 to 99.2.
papers.title_zh: 蒸馏为循环：将预训练扩散 Transformer 转化为具有可调深度的循环模型
papers.abstract_zh: 循环 Transformer 沿网络深度方向复用一块共享权重。近期的循环扩散 Transformer 是从头训练的，尽管已存在强大的预训练非循环扩散 Transformer，这种做法仍重复了完整的预训练成本。我们提出蒸馏为循环（Distill to Loop，Dooop），它将预训练的非循环扩散 Transformer 蒸馏为一个循环学生模型，该学生模型的模块由教师模型的模块初始化。我们将蒸馏表述为朝向教师模型的不动点迭代，其中每一次循环后的输出都被训练以逼近教师模型，而每一次循环都是深度方向上常微分方程的一步。因此，一个模型在测试时可以运行任意数量的循环而无需重新训练，并且扩散模型采样的高阶 ODE 求解器可以沿深度维度应用以获得更好的结果。同时，由于循环模型在每次循环后都会产生一个输出，我们还在不同循环次数的输出之间构造了循环引导，这以极少的额外计算量改善了生成的样本。在 SD3-medium 上，一个参数量约为教师模型 37% 的循环学生模型在两次到四次循环下，在 GenEval、ImageReward、PickScore 和 HPSv2.1 上的平均表现与教师模型相当，而在两次循环下它使用约 58% 的教师模型计算量。而在四步 SD3-medium 上，循环引导将四项指标的平均值从 88.2 提升到 99.2。

papers.title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
papers.summary: Specialist medical vision-language models (VLMs) are strong within their specialties but hard to unify: their training data are often private, and independently developed specialists cannot be assumed to share an architecture. Deploying these large models separately is costly. We present HuluOPD, an on-policy distillation recipe that unifies heterogeneous specialists into one lightweight VLM using only unlabeled prompts, without requiring reference answers or the specialists' training data. The lightweight model answers each prompt, and the specialist of the prompt's modality supervises its response; a continuation-aligned cross-tokenizer loss makes this possible even when they differ in architecture and tokenizer. We apply HuluOPD to five specialists, for ultrasound, pathology, optical coherence tomography, fundus photography, and dental imaging. To distill and evaluate them, we build HuluOPDCorpus, 914k unlabeled prompts, and HuluOPDBench, 47k held-out test items, from over 90 public datasets, and score all models under one protocol on 132k test items, including third-party benchmarks. A single model with 10% of the five specialists' combined parameters retains 94% of their question-answering performance, and one with 2% retains 89%. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of unifying heterogeneous medical specialist VLMs without requiring their training data or a shared architecture.

papers.title: Beyond Before-and-After Images: Evaluating Temporal Grounding in a Lightweight VLM for Disaster Assessment
papers.summary: Bi-temporal satellite imagery is central to disaster assessment: deciding what was damaged requires comparing a pre-event scene with its post-event counterpart. A vision-language model (VLM) can nonetheless appear to answer change questions while relying mainly on the post-event image or on the prompt's temporal framing. We present a controlled diagnostic of temporal grounding and apply it to one lightweight VLM, InternVL3-2B, on DisasterM3: 1,659 optical and SAR image pairs from 41 events and nine disaster types, in event-disjoint partitions, with 9,031 reasoning questions. We compare post-only input, the true pre/post pair, the post image repeated twice, reversed image order, and an unrelated pre-event image. The true pair scores $+0.5$ accuracy points above the repeated-post control (95\% paired bootstrap CI $[-0.2, +1.2]$), and reversing the order changes accuracy by $-0.2$ points ($[-0.8, +0.5]$). Under this protocol we therefore find no measurable benefit from the content of the true pre-event image and little sensitivity to temporal order. The model is not blind to the first image, however: the true pair scores $2.5$ points above a pair whose pre-event image comes from another event ($[+1.6, +3.4]$). State-transition and multi-hop questions remain hard, and optical and SAR inputs show different profiles. We outline temporal scene graphs as a testable next step, not a validated solution, and argue that temporal benchmarks for Earth observation should report whether answers depend on the intended evidence, not only how often they are right.

papers.title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
papers.summary: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while retaining flexibility for non-rigid scene evolution. We also introduce a counterfactual action-faithfulness benchmark covering in-distribution, tail, and out-of-distribution trajectories. On Occ3D-nuScenes, ReCast achieves competitive standard forecasting performance while improving counterfactual forecasting, with particularly clear gains under out-of-distribution trajectories.

papers.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
papers.summary: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for an answer prior and 79.0% for physicians on a subset, and 27 of 32 open models score below 40% on two-way patient-relative directions. Fine-tuning on Clinical3D-45K, our 44,750-question training set, lifts two MLLMs 16-20 points above the best proprietary model. 3D maps given to the fine-tuned MLLM as input go largely unused: replacing them with another video's, even when they are ground truth, barely changes its accuracy. The proposed GeoJeV instead lets the MLLM compute with 3D: it reconstructs a scene memory from each video, selects 3D operations and their arguments from the MLLM's question state, and adds their evidence to its option scores. It achieves the highest accuracy of all evaluated models, narrowing the gap to physicians.
papers.title_zh: Clinical3D-Bench：评估与提升多模态大语言模型在医院环境中的空间智能
papers.abstract_zh: 医院中的空间推理需要追踪外观相似的设备、解读相对于患者的方向，并判断通道宽度，然而现有基准对这些能力的覆盖有限。我们提出 Clinical3D-Bench，一个模拟基准，包含 3,368 个问题、八种类型，基于 373 个医院病房布局的第一人称漫游。布局遵循医院设计指南，答案由 3D 场景计算得到，成对的场景状态测试模型在相关证据变化时是否会改变其答案。视频具有照片级真实感，十名医生筛选了这些布局。在 35 个多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）中，最佳开源模型和专有模型分别达到 45.7% 和 53.6% 的宏准确率，而答案先验为 40.8%，医生在一个子集上为 79.0%，并且 32 个开源模型中有 27 个在双向患者相对方向上得分低于 40%。在 Clinical3D-45K（我们的包含 44,750 个问题的训练集）上进行微调，使两个 MLLM 比最佳专有模型高出 16-20 个百分点。作为输入提供给微调后 MLLM 的 3D 地图在很大程度上未被使用：用另一段视频的 3D 地图替换它们，即使这些地图是真值，也几乎不会改变其准确率。所提出的 GeoJeV 则让 MLLM 使用 3D 进行计算：它从每段视频重建场景记忆，从 MLLM 的问题状态中选择 3D 操作及其参数，并将这些操作的证据加入其选项分数。它在所有被评估模型中取得最高准确率，缩小了与医生的差距。

papers.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback
papers.summary: Text-to-scene methods turn a short instruction into a furnished 3D room, but the room that a particular person wants rarely comes across fully in words: many preferences surface only when the person sees a concrete room and can point to what they like and dislike in it. We therefore study personalized indoor scene synthesis under hidden user preferences: over several turns, a system shows a 3D scene, and the user, who sees only rendered images of the scene, replies with brief free-form feedback and a satisfaction score. The system must therefore bring the whole room toward the user's preferences from feedback that comments on only part of it at a time. It must also be able to change every part of the room, because a preference concerns not only single objects but the look and atmosphere that surfaces, lighting, textiles, furniture and their arrangement create together. We present PreferenceScene, in which a large language model keeps an explicit estimate of the user's preferences for every design attribute of the room and, after each turn, infers the taste behind the feedback and revises the whole estimate, including the parts that the feedback does not mention. A scene instantiation module builds every estimated value as its own part of the room, so that each of these parts can follow the user's preferences. We evaluate on the test set of a benchmark with 320 instances in ten room types, with a simulated user and a render-based evaluator. PreferenceScene matches the hidden preferences better than five published text-to-scene baselines adapted to the same interaction, and its match rises with every turn. It even surpasses them when they are given the preferences directly, and a vision-language model rates its scenes as the most realistic and functional.
papers.title_zh: PreferenceScene：基于反馈的个性化室内场景合成
papers.abstract_zh: 文本到场景方法将简短指令转化为布置好的 3D 房间，但特定的人想要的房间很少能完全用文字表达出来：许多偏好只有在人看到具体房间并能指出其中喜欢和不喜欢之处时才会显现。因此，我们研究隐藏用户偏好下的个性化室内场景合成：在多个轮次中，系统展示一个 3D 场景，而仅看到该场景渲染图像的用户则以简短的自由形式反馈和一个满意度分数进行回复。因此，系统必须从每次只评论房间一部分的反馈中，把整个房间引向用户的偏好。它还必须能够改变房间的每一部分，因为偏好不仅涉及单个物体，还涉及表面、光照、织物、家具及其布置共同创造的外观和氛围。我们提出 PreferenceScene，其中大型语言模型对房间每个设计属性的用户偏好保持显式估计，并在每轮之后推断反馈背后的品味并修订整个估计，包括反馈未提及的部分。场景实例化模块将每个估计值构建为房间中自己的部分，使这些部分中的每一个都能遵循用户偏好。我们在一个包含十种房间类型、320 个实例的基准测试集上进行评估，使用模拟用户和基于渲染的评估器。PreferenceScene 比五个已发表并适配相同交互的文本到场景基线更好地匹配隐藏偏好，并且其匹配度随每一轮提升。即使直接向这些基线提供偏好，它也能超越它们，并且一个视觉语言模型将其场景评为最真实、最实用。

papers.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
papers.summary: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) depicts coronary anatomy and cardiac fat, but segmentation alone does not ensure anatomically consistent measurements. We propose an automated framework that combines deep learning with anatomical reasoning for quantitative cardiac phenotyping. Its anatomical measurement module uses graph geometry, branch identity, and surrounding structures to define vessel-specific pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) sampling and a surrogate epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) compartment. The latter also generates training targets without requiring expert pericardium contours. A companion module quantifies coronary calcium on non-contrast CT. Component-wise benchmarking was conducted on five public datasets: ImageCAS, ImageCAS-X, COCA, Visual Lab, and MultiD4CAD. On ImageCAS-X Test-160, lumen segmentation with validation-selected post-processing achieved a Dice score of 0.9133 and a clDice score of 0.940, exceeding the corresponding published CAS-Net point estimates. In the four-split ImageCAS evaluation, the four-member ensemble outperformed the single ResEnc-L model. Analysis of 800 paired scans showed that PCAT attenuation measurements differed between whole-vessel and lumen references. External EAT evaluation showed strong volume correlation and good spatial overlap. Explicit anatomical rules make the resulting measurements interpretable and inspectable. In practice, the framework provides a standardized pipeline for processing cardiac CT cohorts and quantifying coronary calcium, PCAT, and EAT for population-level analysis and comparison across studies. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/HarryTRAN207/CardiacCT-Research

papers.title: Interpretable Orthogonal Latent Diffusion with Scale-Selective Uncertainty for Medical Image Super-Resolution
papers.summary: Diffusion models are increasingly used for medical image reconstruction and super-resolution, but their samples may contain plausible fine-scale hallucinations that are difficult to identify from the reconstructed image alone. We propose Med-PODiff, a patch-wise proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) diffusion framework for brain MRI super-resolution that performs generative reconstruction in compact and interpretable local coefficient spaces.
